result.title: TouchBench: Can Vision-Language Models Feel Invisible Physical Properties?
result.summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) are increasingly used for embodied perception and reasoning, yet their physical understanding is largely evaluated on questions answerable from images. Many properties critical to manipulation, such as an opaque bottle's fill level or an object's compliance, may only be revealed through touch. We introduce TouchBench, an egocentric vision-language-tactile benchmark that distinguishes visually answerable questions (Tier A) from those involving properties hidden from the camera (Tier B). It pairs head-mounted video with synchronized 137-channel whole-hand tactile sensing, comprising 900 clips from five participants across 11 tasks, with 900 absolute and 4,102 relative questions. Four state-of-the-art VLMs average 66.4% accuracy on Tier A relative questions but only 49.8% on Tier B, near chance (50%). To bridge this gap, we propose Tactile-as-Prompt (TaP), which presents 34 interpretable tactile statistics as text, enabling VLMs to reason with touch without a learned tactile encoder. TaP raises zero-shot Tier B relative accuracy to 62.9% and reaches 73.1% after leave-one-user-out fine-tuning, outperforming video alone (67.4%) and a learned tactile-token encoder (67.3%). The gains extend to unseen objects and users. On a separate 20-hour in-the-wild corpus, tactile text improves fine-tuned contact-question accuracy from 67.1% to 75.5%. These results highlight the limits of vision-only physical reasoning and establish language as an effective interface for tactile perception.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 TouchBench，一个头戴视频与 137 通道全手触觉同步的自中心多模态基准，把可由图像回答的问题（Tier A）与依赖相机外物理属性（Tier B）的问题区分开，并提出将触觉统计以文本提示注入 VLM 的 Tactile-as-Prompt。
AI.relevance_reason: 其 Tier B 诊断显示 VLM 在任务必要信息不在视觉输入时接近随机，且文本接口优于学习式触觉编码器，可供核查「视觉旁路」与任务必要证据如何进入推理状态的问题，但未涉及 latent 推理状态本身。
